fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history: San Fernando Cathedral is an important religious and historical landmark in the city.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: Lazatin Blvd., City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description:
The building has a mini theater, the Mayor's Executive House, the Sangguniang Panlungsod Offices and the Session Hall.

The Heroes Park, meanwhile, houses monuments and markers of Filipino and Fernandino heroes, several of which are listed in the National Historical Commission of the Philippines such as Tiburcio Hilario, Pedro Abad Santos and Jose Abad Santos, among others.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history: Formerly an abandoned warehouse owned by the Technology and Livelihood Resource Center, the property was purchased in 2005 by the City Government of San Fernando, Pampanga during the term of City Mayor Oscar Rodriguez.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: Capitol Blvd., Brgy. Sto. Niño, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: This serves as the seat of the government of the Province of Pampanga.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history: The original building was constructed after the provincial capital of Pampanga was transfered from Bacolor to San Fernando in 1904. It was the site of the major battle between guerilla forces and the Japanese Imperial Army during World War II. The current building dates back to the 1930's.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: Capitol Blvd., Brgy. Sto. Niño, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: Named after former provincial governor Macario Arnedo, it is an important historical landmark and serves as a public venue for relaxation, walking, and civic gatherings. It is most recognized for featuring the monument of revolutionary hero General Maximino Hizon.
A 35.6-hectare, integrated urban township in the heart of San Fernando, Pampanga. It is designed to be the newest Central Business District of Northern and Central Luzon.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history: The township is built on the historic grounds of the former Pampanga Sugar Development Company (PASUDECO), and its master plan integrates residential, commercial, and office components with a focus on preserving the area's rich history and heritage.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: Artemio Macalino St., Brgy. Sto Niño, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history: This structure was among the buildings built in 1907 when the property of the current Provincial Capitol was acquired. It used to house the courts of Pampanga before serving as the Pampanga Provincial Jail.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: The Santungan Ning Kulturang Kapampangan is dedicated to the preservation, promotion, and celebration of the rich history and vibrant heritage of the Kapampangan people. It serves as a comprehensive resource for cultural education and a key driver for heritage tourism in the province.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history: This site served as the ending point of the Death march where Filipino and American prisoners-of-war were forced to march from Bataan to San Fernando. This is considered as one of the ghastliest forced marches in history.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: Brgy. Santo Niño, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the National Historical Commission of the Philippines on April 5, 2005

Inaugurated on February 23, 1892 as part of the Bagbag-Mabalacat stretch of the Manila - Dagupan Railway System by Governor General Eulogio Despujol and Archbishop Bernardino Nozaleda.

Jose Rizal had disembarked from this station on June 27, 1892 to visit his friends in San Fernando and Bacolor, possibly to recruit them as members of the La Liga Filipina.

During the World War II Death March in April 1942, it was the ending point of the 102-kilometer long walk from Bataan to San Fernando by Filipino and American Prisoners of War. From here, the POWs were stuffed into box carts and transported to Capas, Tarlac en route to their final destination, Camp O Donnell.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: A. Consunji St., Brgy. Sto. Rosario, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: A perfect example of the architecture prevalent during the American colonial period.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2003.

Listed in the National Historical Commission of the Philippines on January 26, 2003.

Built by the couple Serafin Lazatin and Encarnacion Singian in 1926, it served as the residence of Japanese General Masaharu Homma during the Japanese occupation of San Fernando. The Lazatins are among the pioneers of the Pampanga Sugar Development Company (PASUDECO) and San Fernando Electric Light and Power Company (SELAPCO).

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: A. Consunji St., Brgy. Sto. Rosario, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2003.

Served as residence of Don Antonio Consunji, Gobernadorcillo of San Fernando, who was removed from office by Spanish authorities as a result of his presence during the visit to San Fernando of Dr. Jose Rizal in June 1892. He became the Presidente Municipal of San Fernando during the Philippine Revolution from 1898-1899.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: This ancestral house, exemplifying the architecture prevalent during the American Colonial Period, is an important heritage edifice of the City.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2003.

The house was designed by Architect Fernando Ocampo and rented to the Tabacalera Company. During the 2nd World War it was appropriated by the Japanese Imperial Army to serve as headquarters of the Kempeitai from 1943-1944.

Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2003.

Originally owned by the couple Victoria Singan and Don Anacleto Hizon, the house was inherited by their daughter, Leoncia Hizon when she married Dr. Basilio Ocampo.

Among the children of the latter born in the residence were Aurea Ocampo Escaler, mother of well-known businessman Ernesto Escaler and Bishop Federico Escaler, SJ.; Arch. Fernando Ocampo, the Father of Modern Filipino Architecture; Sr. Maria Asuncion, RGS, the first Filipina nun of the Religious of the Good Shepherd; twins Pilar Ocampo Feliciano and Rosario Ocampo; Ricardo Ocampo; and Purita Ocampo Gamboa, to whom the house was finally passed on.

Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2003.

Listed in the National Historical Commission of the Philippines on January 26, 2003.

Built in 1870 by Capitan Anacleto Hizon, Gobernadorcillo of San Fernando, and Victoria Singian de Miranda y de Ocampo, it served as headquarters of Spanish General Antonio Ruiz Serralde during the 1896 Philippine Revolution, as military hospital and barracks of the Japanese Imperial Army in 1943-1944, and as headquarters of American General Walter Krueger of the 6th American Army in 1945.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: This ancestral house exemplifying the architecture prevalent during the American Colonial Period.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2003.

Listed in the National Historical Commission of the Philippines on December 2010.

Built at the turn of the century by the couple, Teodoro Santos and Africa Ventura. Purchased by Maria Singian Hizon, a nurse of the Pampanga Chapter of the Philippine Red Cross during the Philippine Revolution. The house was inherited by her nephew Augusto Hizon and is currently owned by his heirs.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: One of the oldest structures in the City, it was once the residence of Andres Eusebio and Asuncion Santos.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
One of the oldest structures in the City, it was once the residence of Andres Eusebio and Asuncion Santos. Being strategically located near the church and casa municipal, it played host to various illustrious personalities including Gen. Douglas Mc Arthur who is said to have stayed overnight in this place.

There are accounts which say that this edifice served as an embarking area, even when it was still a private residence, for many illustrious people especially when there were important events in San Fernando. Being at the crossroad and very close to Baluyut Bridge, the only gateway to the North in the early days, it was a witness to many clashes between the Filipino liberation fighters and the invading enemies. It is said to be the first site of the Pampanga High School and it in this site where the first telephone line was installed in 1910.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: A. Consunji St., Brgy. Sto. Rosario, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: Declared as an Important Cultural Property by the National Museum of the Philippines.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2018.

Declared as an Important Cultural Property by the National Museum of the Philippines.

Founded by the Augustinians in 1754 and placed under the advocation of the Nuestra Senora de la Asuncion while the town was under the patronage of San Fernando III. Fr. Sebastian was named Prior Vicar in 1756.

The stone-church is approximated to have been built in the 18th century. In 1899, both the church and convent were burned by the Philippine Revolutionary Army on order of Gen. Antonio Luna on May 5, 1899. Some 49 years later, in 1948, it was restored through the initiative of Kapampangan Architect Fernando Hizon Ocampo.

Elevated to a Cathedral on December 11, 1948 as the Seat of the newly created Diocese; and on October 1, 1981 it was established as Metropolitan Cathedral under the Titularship of St. Ferdinand and the Patronage of Our Lady of the Assumption.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: A. Consunji St., Brgy. Sto. Rosario, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2003.

The building was built during the Spanish Period in 1874. It was burned by General Antonio Luna during the Philippine American War when the Filipino Revolutionaries retreated amidst the advance of the American forces. It was reconstructed during the American Colonial Period and was completed in 1917 during the administration of Mayor Antonio Abad Santos, under the supervision of District Engineer Eusebius Julius Halsema of the Bureau of Public Works. Restored in 2003 to approximate the design of the century at the time it was built

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: Also known as the "new" public market, is a large, two-story Commercial Center in Downtown San Fernando, Pampanga. As a recent redevelopment of the old public market, it serves as a central hub for commerce and a key component of the city's economic and cultural life.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: General Hizon Avenue, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: The bridge used to serve as the only link of Manila with the rest of Northern Luzon and is recognized as the first concrete pavement in the country.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2003.

Formerly known as Puente Colgante, it was reconstructed in 1696 using iron and stone. It was replaced in 1928 by a reinforced concrete arch bridge design by tormer Philippine Senator and Engineer Sotero Baluyut for his bachelor thesis at the University of lowa in 1909. The bridge used to serve as the only link of Manila with the rest of Northern Luzon and is recognized as the first concrete pavement in the country. The monument of Sotero Baluyut was unveiled on March 30, 2019.

Amando Dayrit Galang, columnist and literary genius was born in this house on February 6, 1912 to Florentino Dayrit Singian and Juana Galang Y Gatchalian, as a writer his name was synonymous with his tribune column "Good Morning Judge," a pre-war series of political criticism which he handled with an equaled wit and humor. Cited as Outstanding Young Man in Literature in February 1941 by Kislap-Graphic. Contributed to the cause of "Free Philippines," a notable underground resistance movement. Due to the rigors of his Journalistic work, he contracted tuberculosis, and while in the hospital, was put under house arrest by the Japanese Imperial Army. Realizing that he had no chance against a worsening illness, he voiced out the wish that if he had to die, he would want to die in his hometown. He was allowed to return to San Fernando, where he died in this house on August 16, 1944.

Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2014.

The original century-old Bahay na Bato owned by Don Pedro Paras, married to Raymunda Mendoza, was inherited by their daughter, Maria Paras, who married Don Ramon Singian Hizon. It was renovated in the 1930s, was razed in a fire in 1950 and immediately rebuilt by Don Ramon Hizon that same year. Rodolfo Hizon, the first Mayor of San Fernando after World War II and later Vice-Governor of Pampanga lived in this house. Eloisa Paras Hizon, married to Domingo M. Gomez, inherited the house. General Maximino Hizon, the Philippine Revolutionary hero, belongs to the same Hizon family tree.

Philippine presidents have been hosted in this ancestral home known as BALE MATUA during their visits to Central Luzon, including Elpidio Quirino, Ramon Magsaysay and Diosdado Macapagal. The young Benigno "Ninoy" Aquino was also an occasional visitor.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: The Henson-Hizon House is a Spanish Colonial period bahay-na-bato built by the couple Don Saturnino Henson y David and Maria Lacson.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2003.

Listed in the National Historical Commission of the Philippines on January 26, 2003.

The Henson-Hizon House is a Spanish Colonial period bahay-na-bato built by the couple Don Saturnino Henson y David and Maria Lacson. Don Saturnino David was gobernadorcillo (mayor) of San Fernando from 1881-1882 and 1896 and the first tesorero municipal (municipal treasurer) from 1900-1902.

Next to the house is a monument dedicated to the heroic efforts of Nicolasa Dayrit-Panilio who helped the sick and wounded Filipino fighters during the Filipino-American War in 1898. She also became instrumental in neutralizing the dispute between Generals Antonio Luna and Tomas Mascardo, when she led a group of female Kapampangans who knelt before General Antonio Luna.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: The architecture features straight-cut design of the colonial period with the year 1938 marked visibly on its façade.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2013.

The two-storey semi-concrete structure owned by couple Angel Y. Datu and Jovita Y. Bundalian was constructed in 1938.

The house was commandeered and occupied by top ranking officers of the Japanese Imperial Army during World War II. It was home to several people such as students and teachers who opted to stay during the school year due its proximity to several educational facilities. Many families who rented the 1st floor had memories to cherish including visits of UNESCO and educational officials.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: The cylindrical structure is reinforced concrete with an approximate height of 95 feet.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2015.

Built during the American Colonial regime in 1921. The structure was erected during the time of Mayor Jose Valencia as part of the first water district in San Fernando.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: Pampanga High School Boulevard, Brgy. Lourdes, City of San Fernando
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the National Historical Commission of the Philippines in August 2018.

Pampanga High School, formerly known as the Jose Abad Santos High School, was founded in 1902 with John W. Osborn as the first principal. It started operations at the Pampanga Hotel. In 1912, the school had its first batch of graduates. In 1935, Demetrio Andres was appointed Principal thereby becoming the first Filipino in that post and the current main building was completed in the same year, following the Standard Plan No. 20 of Gabaldon school houses designed by Architect William E. Parsons.

Among its notable alumni and luminaries are Diosdado Macapagal, former president of the Republic of the Philippines and World War I martyr Jose Abad Santos. The school was named after Jose Abad Santos in 1964 but was reverted back to Pampanga High School in 1992.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: B. Mendoza St., Brgy. Sto. Rosario, City of San Fernando
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history: Built in 1907, the main building of the San Fernando Elementary School followed the Standard Plan No. 20 of Gabaldon school houses designed by American Architect William E. Parsons.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: Brgy. San Jose, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: Designed by Fernando Hizon Ocampo, this former residence of Luis Wenceslao Dizon now houses the residence of the Archbishop of San Fernando and several offices of the Curia of the Archdiocese of San Fernando as well as the Repository Chapel of the canonically crowned image of the Virgen de los Remedios, Patroness of Pampanga and the Santo Cristo del Perdon.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: MacArthur Highway, Dolores, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: Built by the couple Joaquin Dayrit and Maria Paz Cuyugan in 1920, it is a perfect example of the architecture prevalent during the American colonial period.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2003

Listed in the National Historical Commission of the Philippines on January 26, 2003.

Built by the couple Joaquin Dayrit and Maria Paz Cuyugan in 1920, it is a perfect example of the architecture prevalent during the American colonial period.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: B. Mendoza St., Brgy. Dolores, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: The entire sculptural tribute to the people of San Fernando pays homage to the town's colourful history and cultural heritage, as conceptualized by Kapampangan sculptor and Fullbright scholar Abdulmari Toym Imao.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in August 2004.

The iconic monument shows a four-fold aspect of the "Fernandino" story. The Penitent and the Girl with a lantern depicts the unique cultural contributions of the City. The Lady with the Torch reminds us of our freedom and the role of women during the Philippine Revolution. The early settlers are reminiscent of the Kapampangan ancestors who are the people of the river. The boatman who holds an oar and shovel symbolizes the perseverance and resilience of the Fernandino people to cope and triumph over struggles.

Unveiled on February 4, 2004 on the occasion of 3rd City Charter Anniversary of San Fernando.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: Brgy. Del Pilar, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: The restaurant is now owned and operated by the founder's daughter, Petronila S. Jorolan. The establishment which just started with Pancit Luglog and Pancit may sabaw (mami) is also popular for their betute (stuffed frog), adobong camaru (mole cricket), their family's version of the moron, paksiw na bangus with an inch thick of fat, tsokolate batirol and leche flan made with duck eggs.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history: An institution in Kapampangan cuisine founded by Benito and Carmen Santos. They opened their first store in Poblacion San Fernando during the liberation period in the 1940's where everybody can dine, thus the name Everbody's Cafe. In 1967, they opened their branch in Del Pilar.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: Del Pilar Street, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: It is dedicated to the formation of young men for the diocesan priesthood, rooted in the values of human, spiritual, intellectual, and pastoral development. Often referred to by its Latin name, Mater Boni Consilii, it is considered the heart of the archdiocese and has produced a majority of the local clergy, including several bishops.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Founded in 1950 by the first bishop, César María Guerrero, D.D.

Cardinal Pablo Virgilio Siongco David is a prominent figure in the Catholic Church in the Philippines, currently serving as the Bishop of Caloocan. An alumnus of the Mater Boni Consilii Seminary (as it was known during his time, now Mother of Good Counsel Seminary), he served as the President of the Catholic Bishops' Conference of the Philippines (CBCP) until November 2025. He was elevated to the College of Cardinals by Pope Francis on December 7, 2024.

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: 2nd Floor, University of the Assumption, Brgy. San Jose, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: Housed in the University of the Assumption, the museum contains the cultural heritage of the Roman Catholic Church in Pampanga, such as church vessels and vestments, along with exquisite saints and works of art. Reservations with the Archdiocese of San Fernando are required before visiting the museum.

detail_review.name: Heritage Parochial Church, Complex of San Vicente Ferrer

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: Fatima Street, Calulut, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: The complex includes not just the old church structure but also a cemetery, a plaza, century-old artifacts like the 1891 silver reliquary, and intangible heritage such as community devotions and processions.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
Listed in the Local Government Unit Registry of Cultural Properties in 2023.

Originally a chapel from the Spanish colonial period, the church was elevated to the first non-town parish in Pampanga in 1915. It has served as a sanctuary during the Japanese colonial period, a witness to pivotal community events like the assassination of Mayor Levi Panlilio, and a central hub for the religious and cultural life of Calulut and its surrounding areas.

Its history is tied to the lives of many, including prominent figures like Archbishop Pedro Santos and the assassinated Mayor Levi Panlilio.

detail_review.name: City of San Fernando Giant Lantern and Tourist Information Center

fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.address: Former Paskuhan Village Site, Jose Abad Santos Avenue, Brgy. San Jose, City of San Fernando, Pampanga
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.description: On May 27, 2022, the City Government of San Fernando, Pampanga during the leadership of Mayor Edwin D. Santiago, inaugurated the City of San Fernando Giant Lantern and Tourist Information Center at this site as a testament to the enduring Kapampangan cultural heritage and a realization of the City's vision as the Home of the Giant Lanterns.
fields_requiring_pdf_comparison.history:
On this site, the Paskuhan Village, officially known as the Philippine Christmas Village, opened in the City of San Fernando, Pampanga on December 11, 1990 as a tribute to the city's lantern industry and the Giant Lantern Festival. At that time, it was the first theme park in Asia where Christmas was being celebrated the all-year round.

From 1990 to 1998, it served as the official venue for the annual Giant Lantern Festival (Ligligan Parul).

In 1998, Paskuhan became the venue of the Philippine International Garden Festival (FLORIKULTURA'98) and the Gardens of the World

In 2003, Paskuhan was transformed into the North Philippines Cultural and Historical Village known as "WOW Hilaga" and showcased the culture of the locos, Cagayan Valley Central Luzon, and Cordillera Regions.

In 2015, Paskuhan Village was privatized by the Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority and was acquired by the SM Development Corporation.

On January 20, 2020, following a compromise agreement between the City Government of San Fernando, Pampanga and SMDC, the latter donated 5000 square meters of the property and a two-storey building with an outdoor events area.

On May 27, 2022, the City Government of San Fernando, Pampanga during the leadership of Mayor Edwin D. Santiago, inaugurated the City of San Fernando Giant Lantern and Tourist Information Center at this site as a testament to the enduring Kapampangan cultural heritage and a realization of the City's vision as the Home of the Giant Lanterns.
